summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would link Australian trade agreements to labour protections in partner countries, requiring minimum workers’ rights standards to be included in their domestic law.
The benchmarks would draw on eight International Labour Organisation conventions covering association, collective bargaining, discrimination, child labour, working hours, safety and weekly rest.
It would cover agreements reducing or removing Australian tariffs or import charges, and require parliamentary explanation where an exemption from minimum wage standards was made.
changes: The Minister would have to include minimum workers’ rights requirements in relevant trade agreements.
Partner countries would need domestic standards at least equivalent to the minimum wage fixing recommendation, unless an exemption was explained.
The legislation would begin on the day Royal Assent was given.
summary.affected: Workers and employers in Australia’s trading partner countries, those countries’ governments and the Australian Minister responsible for trade agreements are affected.

speeches.speaker: John Madigan
speeches.brief: The Fair Trade (Workers' Rights) Bill 2013 was introduced to require that minimum standards on workers' rights be included in certain international agreements.

speeches.speaker: John Madigan
speeches.brief: The speaker introduced the Fair Trade (Workers' Rights) Bill 2013, arguing that Australian industries cannot compete with imported goods produced under poor labour conditions, and that the bill aims to protect workers' rights and improve competitiveness.
